pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Project's own tests must pass at the end. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

The suite is good, but it fails your gate (overall 9 or more, no item under 7). `npm test` passes: 598 tests, 0 skipped, about 5.6 s. The overall is 8 and duplication scores 6. Bash was blocked when I tried to list `/tmp` and running processes, so I checked cleanup by reading the code, not by inspecting the machine. Every spawned server and temp dir is cleaned up in a `finally` or an `after` hook. **Spec lines with no test or a weak test** 1. **Untested:** "Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`", and the 500 for a missing page file described in api.md. `spawnServer` has a `script` option for this (`test/helpers/server.mjs:43`), but no test uses it. 2. **Weak:** list fetches never get a non-string `error` (should show `Request failed.`) or a body-stream failure. Only the rooms fetch tests these (`app-load-list.test.mjs:165-171`). 3. **Weak:** Cancel never gets a reply whose body fails later (`replyLater(...).fail()`). Only `fail()` and `replyNotJson(404)` are tested. 4. **Can't be tested:** sorting by "room in the order above". The room names are in alphabetical order, so an alphabetical sort can't be told apart. This isn't a test fault. **Flaky timing and hangs** - **No timeout anywhere.** `startServer` waits with no time limit (`helpers/server.mjs:82-91`), and the `npm test` script has no `--test-timeout`. If a server never listens and never exits, the suite hangs forever. Your mutant runner already passes `--test-timeout=30000`; `npm test` should too. - **Unbounded poll loop.** `startup.test.mjs:172` connects again and again until the child exits, with no upper limit. - **Port races.** `freePort()` binds and releases a port and then hands it to the server (`startup.test.mjs:103` and `:165`). The 3000 and 65535 tests have the same race but skip when the port is busy. The risk is low. - **Fixed delays.** `booking-body.test.mjs:258` waits 300 ms and `persistence.test.mjs:172` waits 100 ms. Both only prove that nothing happens, so they can't fail falsely. They could miss a slow bug. **Tests that depend on order within a file** - `api-list.test.mjs`: the DELETE tests change the shared server. The sort and filter tests, and the check at `:134`, expect all 12 bookings, so they must run before them. - `api-list.test.mjs:166`: `assert.ok(ALL_IDS.includes(4))` is always true and checks nothing. - `booking-fields.test.mjs:74-87`: "id 2" and "GET list holds the same objects" only pass after the first test. **Fake DOM fidelity** - **`click()` comment.** At `fake-dom.mjs:101-104` the comment says disabled buttons get no click, but the code dispatches anyway. The behaviour is the stricter one and is useful, so fix the comment. - **Created buttons.** `createElement('button').type` is `''`; a real browser gives `'submit'`. - **Date and time inputs.** They keep invalid values like `2026-11-3` or `9:00`, which a real browser clears to `''`. This is harmless for the "values sent unchanged" tests. - **Moving nodes.** `append` doesn't move a node away from its old parent. **HTML parser** - **Entities.** It never decodes entities like ` ` in text or attributes. - **Implied tags.** It doesn't create implied ``, `

` or `

  • ` tags. - **`` content.** It parses markup inside `<title>` instead of keeping it as plain text. - **Self-closing tags.** `html.mjs:72` mixes `||` and `&&` without brackets, and it treats `<div/>` as closed, which browsers don't. None of these matter for the current `index.html`. **Readability** - Invisible characters are written directly in strings. Examples: the no-break space, U+3000, U+FEFF and U+FFFD at `booking-fields.test.mjs:119,134`, `startup.test.mjs:290` and `booking-body.test.mjs:306`. The combining-accent `é` at `booking-fields.test.mjs:123,132` looks the same as the plain one. Use `\u` escapes. - `failsWith` (`startup.test.mjs:293-299`) returns `name`, which no caller uses, and needs awkward function arguments. **Strengths** - Spec values are compared exactly with `deepStrictEqual`. - Boundary cases are covered well: 10000 and 10001 bytes, multi-byte and chunked bodies, emoji and combining-accent lengths, a no-break space in Content-Type, the byte order mark, invalid UTF-8. - There are good concurrency tests. - The fake DOM blocks every browser API the spec doesn't allow. - The 72 near-miss mutants are realistic. The two scratch scripts are fine. ## GRADE Overall: 8/10 Verdict: fail structure: 8 — files split clearly by area, but shared server state couples tests to their order in api-list and booking-fields naming: 8 — names mostly clear and consistent; `bk`/`B1` (id 2)/`msg`/`sub` are terse and `failsWith` returns a value no caller uses duplication: 6 — uniqueDate/freshBooking, expectError, withServer, exists, boot/errorText/NO_REPLY copied across files; chunkedPost re-implements request() size: 9 — every file under 400 lines, functions short errors: 7 — no startup or test timeout (a hang is possible), unbounded poll loop, JSON.parse throws inside a stream 'end' handler, `exists` swallows every error tests: 8 — strong, exact, and every mutant fails; but the unexpected-500 line is untested, a few frontend cases are missing, and some tests depend on order security: 10 — no secrets, everything runs on 127.0.0.1 in temp dirs leftovers: 9 — no console or TODOs;
